---
title: "Scores API"
---

The scores of the [Scores page](../../index.qmd) are served as files, for every published version, region and track.
On the page, use the **Export** row next to the **Region** and **Track** pickers to download the displayed scores, or to open them in the [EDITO Data Explorer](https://datalab.dive.edito.eu/data-explorer).

## Endpoints

Replace `<version>`, `<region>` and `<track>` with an OceanBench version (for example `0.6.2`), a region identifier (for example `global`) and a track (`high_resolution` or `one_degree`).

| Endpoint | Content |
|---|---|
| `/api/scores/index.json` | The available versions, regions and tracks, with the path of each file |
| `/api/scores/<version>/<region>/<track>.csv` | Scores as CSV |
| `/api/scores/<version>/<region>/<track>.parquet` | Scores as Parquet |
| `/api/scores/<version>/<region>/<track>.zarr` | Scores as a multi-dimensional Zarr store |

Only the combinations listed in `index.json` exist.

## Columns of the CSV and Parquet files

Each row is the score of one challenger, for one metric, depth, variable and lead day.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `version` | OceanBench version |
| `region` | Region identifier |
| `track` | `high_resolution` or `one_degree` |
| `challenger` | Challenger identifier |
| `comparison` | `observations`, `reanalysis` or `analysis` |
| `metric` | Metric title |
| `depth` | Depth range, empty for metrics without depth |
| `variable` | Variable name |
| `standard_name` | CF standard name of the variable |
| `unit` | Unit of the score |
| `lead_day` | Forecast lead day |
| `value` | Score, empty when unavailable |

## Zarr structure

The Zarr store is a dataset with the dimensions `challenger`, `comparison`, `metric`, `depth`, `variable` and `lead_day`.
The `value` array holds the scores, empty where a combination does not exist.
The `unit` and `standard_name` arrays give the unit and CF standard name of each `comparison`, `metric`, `depth` and `variable`.

## Examples

``` bash
curl -O https://oceanbench.edito.eu/api/scores/index.json
curl -O https://oceanbench.edito.eu/api/scores/<version>/global/high_resolution.csv
```

``` python
import pandas
import xarray

scores = pandas.read_parquet("https://oceanbench.edito.eu/api/scores/<version>/global/high_resolution.parquet")
dataset = xarray.open_zarr("https://oceanbench.edito.eu/api/scores/<version>/global/high_resolution.zarr", consolidated=True)
glonet_scores = dataset["value"].sel(challenger="glonet", comparison="reanalysis", metric="Forecasted variables")
```

The Export popup on the Scores page shows these snippets for the displayed version, region and track.

To open the scores in the EDITO Data Explorer, pass the CSV URL as the `source` parameter:

```
https://datalab.dive.edito.eu/data-explorer?source=<url-encoded CSV URL>
```
